availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.name: compact
availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

availableCommands.name: context
availableCommands.description: Show current context usage

availableCommands.name: init
availableCommands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

availableCommands.name: pr-comments
availableCommands.description: Get comments from a GitHub pull request

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: Review a pull request

availableCommands.name: security-review
availableCommands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

availableCommands.name: insights
availableCommands.description: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions

Fix static mode pages not loading data due to project initialization gate
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KK68DSYGW6Y6C0CHJ3FMHV0Q
Type:      task
Status:    pending
Priority:  1
Automation: eligible

─── Description ───
  GitHub Pages static site loads kspec-snapshot.json successfully but no page renders any data. Root cause: +layout.svelte sets appReady=true in static mode but never sets initialized=true in the project store (project.svelte.ts). Every page gates data loading on isProjectInitialized() which returns false forever in static mode. Fix: export a function from project store (e.g. initializeForStaticMode) that sets initialized=true, and call it from +layout.svelte in the static mode branch before setting appReady. Must include E2E regression test verifying that static mode pages render data from the snapshot. Affects all pages: dashboard, tasks, specs, inbox, agents, plans, triage, observations, workflows, sessions, validate, task board.
Spec ref:  @gh-pages-export
Tags:      bug, web-ui, static, gh-pages
Created:   2026-03-08T08:18:39.184Z

─── Spec Context ───
GitHub Pages Export
Type: feature
Implementation: implemented
Description:
  Static site generation from kspec state for hosting read-only views on GitHub Pages.
  CI workflow builds JSON snapshot from shadow branch on push, SPA reads this JSON for rendering.
  Enables deep linking to tasks/specs from PRs and issues with data freshness indicator.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: kspec is installed
    When: user runs 'kspec export --format json'
    Then: writes kspec-snapshot.json containing all tasks, items, inbox, meta to stdout or --output path
  [ac-2]
    Given: export runs
    When: output is generated
    Then: JSON includes exported_at timestamp, version (kspec version), project metadata
  [ac-3]
    Given: export runs
    When: tasks are included
    Then: each task includes resolved spec_ref title (not just ref string) for display without resolution
  [ac-4]
    Given: export runs
    When: items are included
    Then: hierarchical structure preserved, acceptance_criteria expanded, traits resolved to include inherited ACs
  [ac-5]
    Given: export runs with --include-validation
    When: validation is run
    Then: JSON includes validation block with error/warning counts and details
  [ac-6]
    Given: kspec is installed
    When: user runs 'kspec export --format html'
    Then: generates self-contained HTML file with embedded JSON and SPA code
  [ac-7]
    Given: kspec is installed
    When: user runs 'kspec export --dry-run'
    Then: shows what would be exported without writing files
  [ac-8]
    Given: push to kspec-meta branch
    When: CI workflow triggers
    Then: runs kspec export, commits to gh-pages branch
  [ac-9]
    Given: CI workflow runs
    When: SPA assets don't exist
    Then: copies SPA static assets (HTML, JS, CSS) to docs/ alongside JSON
  [ac-10]
    Given: rapid commits to kspec-meta
    When: multiple pushes within 30 seconds
    Then: CI debounces and runs once with latest state
  [ac-11]
    Given: user opens gh-pages URL
    When: SPA loads
    Then: fetches kspec-snapshot.json from same origin, renders dashboard
  [ac-12]
    Given: user navigates to /tasks/@task-slug
    When: deep link resolves
    Then: SPA parses path (history API), shows task detail for that ref
  [ac-13]
    Given: user navigates to /items/@spec-slug
    When: deep link resolves
    Then: SPA shows spec item detail for that ref
  [ac-14]
    Given: SPA renders
    When: validation data present in snapshot
    Then: shows validation summary badge (green check or red X with count)
  [ac-15]
    Given: static export page
    When: displayed to user
    Then: shows 'Data as of: [timestamp]' indicator prominently
  [ac-16]
    Given: viewing task in SPA mode
    When: user sees Start Task button area
    Then: button is disabled with tooltip explaining read-only mode
  [ac-17]
    Given: viewing inbox in SPA mode
    When: Add button area visible
    Then: button is disabled/hidden
  [ac-18]
    Given: SPA mode
    When: any write action attempted
    Then: graceful no-op with informative message
  [ac-19]
    Given: app is built with VITE_STATIC_MODE=true
    When: app initializes on page load
    Then: mode is set to static without attempting daemon health check
  [ac-20]
    Given: app is in static mode
    When: fetching kspec-snapshot.json
    Then: URL is prefixed with SvelteKit configured base path from $app/paths
  [ac-21]
    Given: export runs with validation data available
    When: JSON output is generated for GitHub Pages
    Then: snapshot includes alignment statistics/warnings and detailed validation fields required by the /validate view instead of forcing empty placeholders
  [ac-22]
    Given: the app is in static mode
    When: the user navigates to a sessions route
    Then: the UI shows an informative read-only message instead of failing or implying live session streaming is available
  [ac-23]
    Given: export runs after the web UI adds plans and triage views
    When: JSON output is generated
    Then: snapshot includes read-only plans data (including content and progress fields) and triage records so /plans and /triage can render from static data
  [ac-24]
    Given: the app is in static mode
    When: the user navigates to /settings
    Then: the page renders snapshot-backed sections such as project metadata and conventions, and clearly labels live-only daemon/shadow details as unavailable
  [ac-25]
    Given: The app is in static mode after initMode() completes and snapshot JSON is loaded
    When: A page component checks project initialization before loading data
    Then: The project store reports initialized=true so that page-level data loading gates (isProjectInitialized) pass and static API functions can serve snapshot data to all views

─── Inherited from @trait-json-output ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: command supports JSON mode
    When: --json flag is provided
    Then: output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
  [ac-2] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: JSON mode is active
    When: command completes successfully
    Then: output includes all data available in human-readable mode
  [ac-3] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: JSON mode is active
    When: command encounters an error
    Then: error is returned as JSON object with error field
  [ac-4] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: JSON output contains references
    When: output is generated
    Then: references use @ prefix consistently
  [ac-5] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: JSON output contains timestamps
    When: output is generated
    Then: timestamps use ISO 8601 format
  [ac-6] (from @trait-json-output)
    Given: command supports --json
    When: used with other formatting flags
    Then: --json takes precedence over other format options

─── Inherited from @trait-dry-run ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-dry-run)
    Given: command supports dry run
    When: --dry-run flag is provided
    Then: show what would be changed without applying
  [ac-2] (from @trait-dry-run)
    Given: dry run mode is active
    When: command completes
    Then: no files are modified
  [ac-3] (from @trait-dry-run)
    Given: dry run mode is active
    When: output is shown
    Then: clear indication that this is a preview
  [ac-4] (from @trait-dry-run)
    Given: dry run mode is active
    When: command would error
    Then: error shown but no state changed
  [ac-5] (from @trait-dry-run)
    Given: --dry-run and --force both provided
    When: command executes
    Then: dry run takes precedence (no changes made)
  [ac-6] (from @trait-dry-run)
    Given: dry run in JSON mode
    When: --dry-run --json provided
    Then: JSON output includes dry_run boolean field
